title: Semilinear normal projective Galois domination of an alteration
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and $H$ a finite group acting on $S$ and $k$ compatibly. Let $r:T\to S$ be any alteration, with $T$ integral. There exist a finite group $J$, a surjection $\rho:J\to H$, a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $W$, a $J$-action on $W$ compatible with the action on $k$ through $\rho$, an equivariant H-projective alteration $b:W\to S$, and an $S$-morphism $t:W\to T$ with $rt=b$. Put $N=\ker\rho$. Then $k(W)^N/k(S)$ is finite purely inseparable. No action on $T$ is required. The extension $k(W)/k(S)$ is finite; if $k(T)/k(S)$ is separable, $W$ can be chosen with $k(W)/k(S)$ separable and $k(W)^N=k(S)$.

Field, integral scheme, proper morphism, finite type, geometric integrality, projectivity, finite morphism, surjectivity, function field and field extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target; it does not refer to a group named H. A normal scheme has integrally closed domains as local rings. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes, finite over a dense open of the target. A purely inseparable extension in characteristic p>0 means that every element has some p-power in the smaller field; in characteristic zero it means equality. All group actions below are by scheme or field automorphisms, and are allowed to be nonfaithful.

source.place: de Jong (1997), §§3.2 and 3.8, pp.605,608, and Situation 5.3, p.613; general semilinear conjugate-product/projective-domination form of ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4, pp.160--161. Nonseparable extensions use the purely inseparable-then-Galois convention of ILO X Remark 3.3.2, p.158. Local de Jong PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.

proof.text: Put $K=k(S)$ and $L=k(T)$; the dense-open finiteness of $r$ makes $L/K$ finite. Apply the finite semilinear field envelope to $A_h=(h^{-1})^*$ on $K$. It gives $M$, the finite group $J$ of compatible pairs, and $\rho:J\twoheadrightarrow H$; its kernel is $\operatorname{Aut}_K(M)$. Keep its separable choice when $L/K$ is separable.

source.place: Re-split assembly of the original semilinear domination construction, ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4, pp.160--161.

proof.text: Let $J$ act on $S$ and $k$ through $\rho$ and on $M$ through its second coordinate. The finite-normalization-model lemma gives a normal integral projective $k$-scheme $B$ finite over $S$, with generic fibre $\operatorname{Spec}M$ and the specified semilinear action.

source.place: Re-split assembly of the original semilinear domination construction, ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4, pp.160--161.

proof.text: The alteration $r$ is a proper $k$-morphism and $T$ is integral of finite type over $k$. Its generic fibre is $T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K=\operatorname{Spec}L$: over a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subseteq S$ over which $r$ is finite, $r^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A_0)=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ with $B_0$ a domain finite over $A_0$, and $B_0\otimes_{A_0}K$ is the localization of $B_0$ at $A_0\setminus\{0\}$, a domain finite over the field $K$, hence a field, equal to $\operatorname{Frac}B_0=L$. Fix the inclusion $L\subseteq M$ of the tower of step 1. Apply the conjugate-projective-generic-closure lemma to $B\to S$, $r:T\to S$ and $L\hookrightarrow M$. It supplies a projective birational model $\pi:Y\to T$, the integral projective reduced graph closure $C$, its compatible $J$-action, its equivariant map $p:C\to S$, and $c:C\to Y$ with $r\pi c=p$. The generic fibre of $C$ is $\operatorname{Spec}M$, with the original action.

source.place: Re-split assembly of the original semilinear domination construction, ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4, pp.160--161.

proof.text: Normalize $C$ using the equivariant-projective-model-normalization lemma. This gives normal integral projective $W$, the lifted action and the equivariant H-projective alteration $b=p\nu$. Set $t=\pi c\nu:W\to T$. Since $v=r\pi$ and $vc=p$, associativity gives $rt=b$. The generic-field identification is equivariant, so the field-envelope conclusions give $k(W)^N/K$ finite purely inseparable and $k(W)/K$ finite. Its separable choice gives $k(W)/K$ separable and $k(W)^N=K$.

source.place: Re-split assembly of the original semilinear domination construction, ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 4, pp.160--161.
